doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Eddie South, high school and the South Side scene
title: Playing with Freddie Keppard
summary: Hinton remembers Keppard as a powerhouse trumpeter, older and ill when they played at a Bingham State Bank ballroom at 35th and State.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: It was too late then. But I had played with Freddy Kephard.
Tell me about Freddy Kephard. How did he compare to Louis Armstrong? I‟ve heard people talk about that.
He was a powerhouse. He didn‟t have as much creativity as…
He had power. You could hear him two miles away. He was a big man, tall, but when I played with him he was on his…

He was older and he was getting sick. He lived right near me, 35th and State Street, just… Bingham… [unintelligible] had a bank, Bingham State Bank. He‟d opened a new building, a new office building at 35th and State and they had a ballroom there and he got the job as a bandleader.
